How Much Does Commercial Renovation Cost in Vancouver & Metro Vancouver in 2026?

Commercial renovation costs in Vancouver and Metro Vancouver in 2026 range from $8,000 for a single-entry warehouse door replacement to over $360,000 for a full-scale clinic build-out. Most retail, office, and clinic fit-outs fall between $150 and $350 per square foot, depending on scope, materials, and the city where the project is located. A small retail refresh takes two to three weeks; a complete professional clinic renovation can run four to five months.

These are not estimates — they come from Reno Stars Construction projects completed in Burnaby, Vancouver, and across Metro Vancouver in 2025 and 2026. This guide breaks down real costs by project type, explains what drives the price, and shows you what a budget for your commercial renovation in Metro Vancouver should actually look like.

What Qualifies as a Commercial Renovation in BC

A commercial renovation in British Columbia is any renovation to a space that generates revenue — a retail store, office, clinic, restaurant, warehouse, or personal-care business. Unlike residential work, commercial projects in BC must comply with the BC Building Code, local municipal bylaws, and in some cases WorkSafeBC requirements. Permits are typically required when structural changes, electrical upgrades, or plumbing modifications are involved.

The key difference from residential renovation is operational impact: every day a clinic is closed is lost revenue. That changes the priority from "doing it right" (still essential) to "doing it on time." Experienced commercial contractors in Vancouver and Burnaby know how to phase work, work after hours, and compress schedules without cutting corners on safety or code compliance.

What Drives Commercial Renovation Cost in Vancouver and Burnaby

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars.

Four factors determine where your project's budget lands within that range.

  • Scope of work: A targeted refresh — new paint, flooring, and millwork — costs a fraction of a full structural reconfiguration. The dental clinic in Burnaby was completed in one week because the scope was defined narrowly and decisions were made quickly.
  • Materials and finishes: Professional clinics and retail spaces typically require durable commercial-grade materials that last under high traffic. The skin lab in Vancouver invested in custom millwork and optimized recessed lighting for treatment rooms — both add cost but reduce long-term maintenance.
  • Permit and inspection requirements: Burnaby, Vancouver, and other Metro Vancouver municipalities have specific commercial occupancy requirements. Accessibility upgrades (such as the accessible washroom at the Vancouver skin lab) are frequently required and must meet City of Vancouver or municipal bylaws.
  • Schedule pressure: Speed kills cost. When a client needs a clinic open in one week instead of three, contractors pull long hours, sequence trades tightly, and pay a premium for urgency. The dental clinic renovation in Burnaby is a clear example: a one-week deadline for a project that would normally take three weeks required 24-hour execution.

Permits and Inspections for Commercial Renovations in Metro Vancouver

Commercial renovations in Vancouver, Burnaby, and across BC require one or more of the following permits:

  • Building Permit: Required for any structural change, change of occupancy, or work that affects fire safety, accessibility, or structural integrity.
  • Electrical Permit: Issued by Technical Safety BC. Required when adding circuits, changing panel capacity, or modifying wiring in a commercial space.
  • Plumbing Permit: Required for new or relocated plumbing fixtures, especially in clinics and personal-care spaces where equipment requires specific hookups.
  • Sign Permit: Often required separately in Vancouver and Burnaby for exterior signage changes associated with a renovation.

The City of Vancouver and City of Burnaby both require a building permit application before work begins on most commercial interiors. Processing times vary: a simple retail refresh may be approved in days; a clinic reconfiguration requiring accessibility upgrades can take two to four weeks. Reno Stars handles permit applications as part of the project management scope, coordinating with city inspectors and Technical Safety BC.

How Long Does a Commercial Renovation Take in Vancouver?

Timeline depends entirely on scope and whether permits are involved.

  • Minor refresh (paint, flooring, millwork): 1–3 weeks. The Metrotown toy store completed in 2–3 weeks.
  • Moderate renovation (electrical, plumbing, layout changes): 3–8 weeks.
  • Full fit-out or clinic renovation: 1–6 months. The Vancouver skin lab took 4–5 months for a complete redesign.

One critical consideration for clinic and retail owners: partial occupancy may be possible during renovation. In some cases, a contractor can phase the work so part of your space remains operational while other areas are being renovated. This is especially common in multi-room clinics and large retail spaces.

What Does a 2026 Commercial Renovation Budget Look Like for Metro Vancouver?

Based on completed Reno Stars projects, here are realistic budget benchmarks for commercial renovation in Vancouver and Burnaby in 2026.

Project ScaleEstimated Budget (2026)Typical Timeline
Entry/doorway refresh$8,000–$15,000Less than 1 week
Small retail or salon refresh$20,000–$50,0002–4 weeks
Medium clinic or professional office$80,000–$200,0001–3 months
Large full-scope commercial fit-out$300,000–$400,000+3–6 months

These figures include labour, materials, and permit-related fees. They do not include furniture, equipment, or signage unless those items were part of the specific project scope. A dentist relocating into a new shell space, for example, would need to budget separately for dental chairs, X-ray equipment, and specialized plumbing.

Frequently Asked Questions About Commercial Renovation Costs in Vancouver

How much does a clinic renovation cost in Vancouver?

A dental or skin care clinic renovation in Vancouver or Burnaby typically costs between $150 and $350 per square foot depending on scope. A 1,500-square-foot clinic renovation in Vancouver with custom millwork, updated electrical, and an accessible washroom can reach $345,000–$360,000. Smaller clinic refreshes — new flooring, paint, and millwork — may cost $80,000–$150,000.

Do I need a permit for a commercial renovation in Burnaby or Vancouver?

Yes. Most commercial interior renovations in Vancouver and Burnaby require a building permit. Electrical and plumbing work require separate permits from Technical Safety BC and the municipal authority. The only exceptions are minor cosmetic work that does not affect structural elements, fire safety systems, or building code compliance. Always check with the City of Vancouver or City of Burnaby building department before starting work.

Can I do a commercial renovation while staying open for business?

It depends on your layout. Single-room spaces — a small retail kiosk or a one-room clinic — typically need to close during work. Multi-room clinics and larger retail spaces can often phase work room by room or zone by zone, remaining partially operational. Reno Stars has experience sequencing work to minimize revenue impact for clinic and retail clients in Burnaby and Vancouver.

What is the biggest cost driver in a commercial renovation in Metro Vancouver?

Scope changes mid-project are the most common cost driver. Clients who finalize their layout, materials, and finishes before awarding the contract consistently come in closer to budget. The dental clinic renovation in Burnaby — completed in one week — worked because the scope was defined and locked before work began. The Vancouver skin lab project stayed on budget at $345,000–$360,000 for a four-to-five-month full redesign because the design was resolved early.

How do I budget for a retail renovation in Metro Vancouver in 2026?

Start with a realistic cost-per-square-foot estimate ($150–$350 depending on scope), add 10–15% contingency for unknowns, and confirm permit fees with your municipality. Obtain at least two contractor quotes with detailed scopes of work. The toy store renovation in Metrotown, Burnaby — $23,000–$25,000 for structural modifications, commercial laminate flooring, and a full interior repaint — illustrates what a mid-range retail project looks like in the current Metro Vancouver market.

Is Vancouver or Burnaby more expensive for commercial renovation?

Vancouver tends to have higher permit fees and longer processing times, which can add cost to complex projects. Burnaby's permit process is often slightly faster for straightforward commercial interior renovations. Material and labour costs are comparable across the two cities. For large-scale projects where time is money, Burnaby's faster permit turnaround can translate to a lower total cost.
